instagram_caption:
🚀 The iPhone vs Android Timeline: when the market slowed, Apple didn’t.

In 2019, global smartphone share looked like “normal” Android dominance: Apple sat at 16.2% while Android’s ecosystem was led by Samsung at 20.8%. Shipments were ~1.38B units, so everyone had room to breathe.

Then 2020 hit. Shipments stayed near flat at ~1.37B, but consumer behavior shifted and Apple used the moment: iPhone share jumped to 18.9% (from 16.2%). Samsung’s Android share barely moved (20.4%), while the “Other Android OEM” bucket slipped to 58.1%—the first sign that fragmentation was costing leverage.

By 2021, the rebound turned into a real split. Apple climbed to 21.0% as shipments rose to ~1.45B. Samsung fell to 18.8%, and “Other Android OEMs” consolidated risk: 56.8%. In other words—when demand increased, Apple gained share, but Android couldn’t keep the same momentum everywhere.

The dramatic turn came in 2022–2023 as the smartphone market cooled. Shipments dropped from ~1.25B (2022) to ~1.17B (2023). During that contraction, Apple didn’t crack—its share went from 24.1% to 24.5%. Samsung, meanwhile, slid to 18.5% in 2023, while the rest of Android hovered near 57%—broad reach, weaker power.

Fast-forward to the 2024–2025 AI upgrade cycle. Shipments bottomed near ~1.17B in 2023 and recovered to ~1.23B in 2024—yet iPhone share kept climbing: 25.2% in 2024 and ~26.0% by 2025. Samsung stayed stuck around 18% and then 17.2%, while “Other Android OEMs” held steady at ~56.8%.

So here’s the viral question: 👇
Do you think Apple’s advantage is brand + ecosystem lock-in… or is Android’s problem mainly fragmentation?

facebook_caption:
Apple’s iPhone strengthened its position as the global smartphone market moved from pandemic-era normalization into a multi-year contraction. In 2019, Apple held 16.2% global share; by 2021 it reached 21.0%, while Samsung (leading Android) slipped to 18.8% in 2021.

The turning point was the demand cooling phase. Total annual shipments fell from ~1.45B units in 2021 to ~1.25B in 2022 and ~1.17B in 2023. During this contraction, Apple expanded further—from 24.1% in 2022 to 24.5% in 2023—indicating resilience when budgets tightened. Samsung’s share declined to 18.5% in 2023, while “Other Android OEMs” remained broadly stable near ~57%.

By 2024–2025, the market recovered modestly (shipments ~1.23B in 2024, ~1.22B in 2025), but share gains continued to favor Apple: ~25.2% in 2024 and ~26.0% in 2025. Samsung stayed pressured around ~18.0% in 2024 and ~17.2% in 2025, reinforcing a high-level theme: when the market tightens, consolidation and ecosystem pull can outcompete fragmented competition.

Hot take: Android didn’t lose because it “failed”—it lost because it’s a crowd.

Apple’s iPhone share went 16.2% (2019) → 21.0% (2021) → 24.5% (2023) → ~26% (2025). Meanwhile Samsung peaked around 20% and slid down to ~17.2% by 2025. Shipments also cooled hard: ~1.45B (2021) → ~1.17B (2023).

So when the market shrank, Apple got even stronger. That’s the story.

Do you think Apple’s edge is ecosystem/brand… or are Android OEMs trapped by too many overlapping models?
